titleEn: Sit to Eat, Run to Play!

pages.text: "It's cooler outside!" Rudi the hungry squirrel hopped over the doorstep with corn in hand. Five places on the long bench, five ears of corn. Only Rudi's seat was empty.
"Eating and playing together is much more fun!" Holding the corn, Rudi hopped out again. "Once I'm done, I'll be first up the apple tree!"
Yellow kernels lay scattered on the dirt by the step. Rudi hopped over them again. Leo said, "You'll fall doing that." Rudi pretended not to hear.
Then Rudi's big tail caught on the doorstep. Rudi fell forward. The corn slipped from their hand and rolled across the dirt.
When Rudi picked it up, it was rough with soil. On the bench, the four had finished and stood up. Rudi sat on the doorstep, hugging their big tail.
Grandma Bear came and sat beside Rudi without a word. She broke her corn in half and put one half in Rudi's hand. Then she sat with her feet together and chewed.
Rudi sat firmly beside Grandma too. Sitting to eat, not a kernel fell. Grandma said quietly, "Sit to eat, run to play!"
Crunching right to the last kernel, Rudi finished. Only the white cob remained. "All eaten! Now it's time to run!" Waving the cob, Rudi hopped over the step.
At lunch the next day, Rudi sat on the bench first. "One, sit to eat! Two, finish, then stand! Three, then run all I want!" Leo sat firmly in the next place too.
Grandma stroked Rudi's back. "Not a thing spilled today." Run while eating, and food gets dirty. Sit to eat, and you finish every bit. "Sit to eat, run to play!" Rudi waved their tail.
